source: Zhang et al. (2025/2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Distilled strategy items beat raw-trajectory memory (Synapse) and success-only workflow memory (AWM) on WebArena across three backbones. This is the nearest test of gap 1.
numbers: WebArena overall SR, 684 tasks, pass@1. Gemini-2.5-flash: no memory 40.5, Synapse (raw trajectories) 42.1, AWM 44.1, ReasoningBank 48.8, +MaTTS 51.8. Gemini-2.5-pro: 46.7 / 47.7 / 47.6 / 53.9 / 56.3. Claude-3.7-sonnet: 41.7 / 42.6 / 40.8 / 46.3 / 48.8. Steps fell from 9.7 to 8.3 (flash).
limits: Not token-matched: prompt tokens per arm not reported. Success labels come from an LLM judge. Backbones are 2025 models without extended-thinking settings. Authors are the method authors.
agent_relevance: Supports a distilled-lesson S0 class record over raw earlier solutions. Gain over raw is about 3 to 6 points, over no memory 5 to 8 points.

source: Zhang et al. (2025/2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Learning from failed runs adds value only when the extraction step is built for it. Baselines gained almost nothing from failures.
numbers: Text: Synapse rose only from 40.6 (success only) to 41.7 (with failures); ReasoningBank rose from 46.5 to 49.7 (WebArena ablation as reported).
limits: One ablation figure; exact subset and backbone not fully stated in the extracted text.
agent_relevance: A class record should store failure lessons as written prevention rules, not as raw failed traces.

source: Zhang et al. (2025/2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Write gating by a noisy judge still helps. The judge was only 72.7% accurate and performance was flat between 70% and 90% simulated judge accuracy. Best at 100%.
numbers: WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash judge. Real judge accuracy 72.7% against ground truth. Simulated accuracies 100, 90, 80, 70, 60, 50 percent by flipping labels. Success rates in the figure fall roughly in a 47 to 53 band against 39.0 for no memory on that subset (read from a garbled figure; approximate).
limits: Simulation flips labels at random; real judge errors are correlated with hard tasks. One subset, one judge.
agent_relevance: Answers part of gap 2: a verifier near 70% accuracy was enough here, if failures are stored as lessons. Contrast with Reflexion Rust test omission (b12).

source: Zhang et al. (2025/2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: On SWE-Bench-Verified the gain is smaller, and raw-trajectory memory can lose to no memory.
numbers: Resolve rate: Gemini-2.5-flash no memory 34.2, Synapse 35.4, ReasoningBank 38.8; Gemini-2.5-pro no memory 54.0, Synapse 53.4, ReasoningBank 57.4.
limits: Single run per cell; no confidence interval.
agent_relevance: Raw earlier solutions can be neutral or harmful on strong models; distilled items gave +3.4 to +4.6.

source: Zhang et al. (2025/2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
finding: Success-only workflow memory can hurt on transfer. AWM fell below no memory on the Multi-site subset and for Claude overall.
numbers: WebArena Multi subset (29 tasks), flash: no memory 10.3, AWM 3.4, ReasoningBank 13.8. Claude-3.7 overall: no memory 41.7, AWM 40.8, ReasoningBank 46.3.
limits: Multi subset is tiny, so one task is 3.4 points.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition for K10 and K11: store type matters; a bad store is worse than none.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners (AAAI 2024)
finding: Both parts matter: extracted insights and retrieved successful examples. Which matters more depends on the task. Insight upvote and downvote counts prune bad insights.
numbers: HotpotQA insights-only 36% vs retrieve-only 31%; ALFWorld 50% vs 55%; WebShop 37% vs 38% (SR). Insight ablation HotpotQA SR: ReAct 28.0, hand-crafted insights 32.0, insights with reflections added 29.0, gpt-3.5 insights 32.0, full ExpeL 39.0. ALFWorld example retrieval: ReAct 40.0, reason-similarity 48.5, random 42.5, task-similarity (ExpeL) 59.0. ExpeL without retries matches Reflexion at round 3 on HotpotQA (40% vs 39%) and trails it on ALFWorld (54% vs 59%).
limits: gpt-3.5 actor, gpt-4-0613 insight extractor, 2023. Adding reflections to insight extraction hurt (hallucinated reflections misled extraction). Standard errors about 0.3 to 2 points.
agent_relevance: Direct cue-design evidence for gap 3: retrieval key choice moved ALFWorld success by up to 16.5 points (59.0 vs 42.5 random). Importance counts are a cheap in-context analogue of Soar-RL numeric preferences.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
finding: A curated, rewritten cheatsheet gives large gains where one reusable trick exists, and small or negative ones elsewhere.
numbers: Baseline / DC-Cumulative / DC-Retrieval-Synthesis. Claude 3.5 Sonnet: AIME 2024 23.3 / 50.0 / 46.7; AIME 2025 6.7 / 36.7 / 30.0; GPQA-Diamond 59.6 / 61.1 / 68.7; MMLU-Pro Eng 61.2 / 66.8 / 67.6. GPT-4o: Game of 24 10 / 93 / 99; AIME 2024 20.0 / 36.7 / 40.0; MMLU-Pro Eng 53.2 / 44.0 / 51.2; MMLU-Pro Physics 75.6 / 70.4 / 75.2. Claude Game of 24 12 / 14 / 14.
limits: Sequential test streams, no ground-truth labels. AIME sets are 30 problems, so one problem is 3.3 points. GPT-4o loses on MMLU-Pro under DC-Cu.
agent_relevance: Supports distilled records when a solved pattern recurs (code snippets, formulas). Tasks without recurrence gain little.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
finding: Full-history appending (all earlier turns raw in context) is worse than curated memory and can be worse than no memory. Direct answer to gaps 1 and 4 for models of that era.
numbers: AIME 2024: Claude 3.5 Sonnet baseline 23.3, full history 26.7, DC 50.0; GPT-4o baseline 20.0, full history 6.7, DC-RS 40.0. Uncurated dynamic retrieval of raw pairs: GPT-4o 26.7 vs 40.0 for DC-RS; Claude 43.3 vs 46.7.
limits: Not token-matched; full history uses far more tokens. 30-problem sets, one run.
agent_relevance: When history fits in context, raw appending is not a free baseline: it can hurt. A curated record is the better default.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
finding: Reasoning-tuned and small models gained little or inconsistently from the cheatsheet. This is the only direct evidence found for gap 9.
numbers: Text: smaller models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.5 Haiku) show limited gains; DeepSeek R1 and o1 experiments showed minimal or inconsistent improvements.
limits: No numbers for R1 or o1 in the text read. Reason offered: verbose solutions and weak strategy writing. Pre-2026 models, thinking budgets not varied.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 stays partly open: memory may help weaker or non-thinking models more. Test our record with and without extended thinking.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models (ICLR 2026)
finding: Rewriting the whole memory each time collapses it. Append small deltas with counters instead. A detailed playbook beats a short summary.
numbers: Context collapse case on AppWorld: step 60 context 18,282 tokens at accuracy 66.7; next step 122 tokens at 57.1, below the no-adaptation baseline 63.7. ACE vs GEPA offline: 82.3% lower adaptation latency, 75.1% fewer rollouts; online FiNER vs Dynamic Cheatsheet: 91.5% lower latency, 83.6% lower token cost.
limits: Authors own case study; DeepSeek-V3.1 non-thinking mode.
agent_relevance: Class record must be edited by small additions with usage counters, never fully rewritten by the model.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models (ICLR 2026)
finding: Write gating needs a reliable feedback signal. With code-execution feedback the playbook helps without labels; without reliable feedback it can degrade. Answers gap 2 (minimum verifier).
numbers: AppWorld DeepSeek-V3.1: online ACE beats Dynamic Cheatsheet by 7.6 points on average; without ground-truth labels ACE still averages +14.8 over the ReAct baseline (execution success or failure as signal). Finance: ACE +10.9 offline over ICL, MIPROv2, GEPA; +6.2 over DC online.
limits: Paper says that with no ground truth or reliable execution signal, both ACE and DC may degrade as the context is polluted. No number given for that case.
agent_relevance: Minimum verifier is a hard programmatic check (code ran, answer matched). Soft self-judgement alone is not shown safe.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models (ICLR 2026)
finding: Gains replicate on a newer model. GPT-5.1 still gains about 11 points on AppWorld with ACE.
numbers: AppWorld test-normal GPT-5.1 base TGC 61.9, SGC 46.4, average 54.2. Online ACE: TGC 72.6 (+10.7), SGC 58.9 (+12.5), average 65.8 (+11.6). Offline ACE average 61.3 (+7.1). Across four model families gains are mostly 5 to 12 points.
limits: GPT-5.1 reasoning effort not stated in the text read. Table extraction garbled; figures read from table rows.
agent_relevance: Memory benefit persisted on a 2025 frontier model; supports a modest yes on gap 9 for agent tasks, not for pure reasoning.

source: Krishnamurthy, Harris, Foster, Zhang, Slivkins (2024) Can Large Language Models Explore In-Context? (NeurIPS 2024)
finding: LLMs do not balance trying options and using the best one by themselves. Only an externally computed per-option summary of outcomes plus a hint plus chain of thought worked. This is the in-context version of Soar-RL operator values (gap 5).
numbers: Bandits K=5 gap 0.2 (hard), K=4 gap 0.5 (easy). 48 configs each for GPT-3.5 and Llama2, 72 for GPT-4; only one worked: GPT-4 + suggestive hint + history summarised to per-arm averages + zero-shot CoT (T=200, N=40). Basic GPT-4 prompt (T=500, N=20): over 60% of replicates chose the best arm only about half the time or less. Same winning prompt without the summary failed.
limits: Bernoulli bandits only, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama2. No state. Does not test operator choice in a real agent.
agent_relevance: Keep outcome counts per operator as code-computed summaries in context; do not ask the model to tally history. Whether this beats fixed operator order is untested (gap 5 partly open).

source: Wang, Mao, Fried, Neubig (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Reusable workflows induced from earlier runs help on web tasks against strong baselines.
numbers: Relative success gains 24.6% (Mind2Web step-wise) and 51.1% (WebArena, over the BrowserGym baseline); online AWM beats baselines by 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points as train-test gap widens; 7.6% relative over human-written workflows.
limits: In ReasoningBank reruns AWM fell below no memory in places (d05). 2024 models.
agent_relevance: Supports abstracted routines; note instability across backbones.

source: Tan et al. (2025) In Prospect and Retrospect: Reflective Memory Management for Long-term Personalized Dialogue Agents
finding: Retrieval quality is the bottleneck. Oracle retrieval is far above any practical retriever; adapting retrieval from the model cited evidence closes part of the gap. Answers gap 3 for dialogue memory.
numbers: LongMemEval accuracy (Gemini-1.5-Flash): oracle retrieval 90.2; RAG Contriever 58.8, Stella 61.4, GTE 63.6; RMM 61.2 / 64.8 / 70.4; Recall@5 with GTE 62.4 vs RMM 69.8. A long-context row reads 57.4 accuracy (table text interleaved; approximate). Ablation: topic-based memory alone 59.6; retrieval refinement without reranker 60.2.
limits: Retriever fine-tuned with a reranker; needs training data. Table extraction garbled in places. Dialogue memory, not agent action memory.
agent_relevance: Cue design is worth about 6 to 12 points here, and about 20 points remain up to oracle (70.4 to 90.2). A cue with state and proposed operator is plausible but unmeasured.

source: Hsieh et al. (2024) RULER: What is the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
finding: Claimed context length overstates usable length. The crossover where a store beats full context depends on task complexity.
numbers: 17 models, 4K to 128K. GPT-4 claimed 128K, effective 64K (96.6 at 4K, 87.0 at 64K, 81.2 at 128K). Llama3.1-70B effective 64K; Qwen2-72B 32K; Mistral-v0.2 7B 16K; only Gemini-1.5-Pro beyond 128K (94.4 at 128K).
limits: Synthetic tasks, 2024 models. Not agent memory.
agent_relevance: For gap 4, a store pays off once history exceeds the model effective length; below about 32K tokens full context is competitive (Mem0 paper full context 72.9, see K11).

source: Yan et al. (2026) Memory-R1: Enhancing LLM Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
finding: A learned memory manager (ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, NOOP) helps, and its quality limits downstream gains.
numbers: LoCoMo, 152 training questions, LLaMA-3.1-8B: removing the RL-trained manager (PPO) lowers F1, BLEU-1, J from 41.0, 32.9, 57.5 to 34.5, 28.1, 49.0. Answer-agent gain with LLaMA manager F1 +10.10, J +5.05; with GPT-4o-mini manager F1 +19.72, J +15.76. Relative gains 28% F1, 34% BLEU-1, 30% J over baseline.
limits: Needs weight training; LoCoMo only, zero-shot transfer to MSC and LongMemEval. No isolated delete-vs-keep number.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: memory operations including DELETE matter, but no isolated effect. Gap 2: store quality compounds downstream.

source: Zhong et al. (2024) MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory (AAAI 2024)
finding: Ebbinghaus-style forgetting and reinforcement were built, but the quantitative table has no forgetting-off ablation.
numbers: 194 probing questions on simulated dialogs. English: SiliconFriend ChatGPT retrieval accuracy 0.763, correctness 0.716, coherence 0.912; ChatGLM 0.809, 0.438, 0.68; BELLE 0.814, 0.479, 0.582.
limits: Simulated users by ChatGPT; cannot tell if forgetting helped. Gap 7 evidence stays thin.
agent_relevance: Do not copy a forgetting curve into the record untested; history-based deletion (Xiong, b20) is better evidence.

source: Gorski and Laird (2011) Learning to use episodic memory; Nason and Laird (2005) Soar-RL
